<ul> <li>Dispersion games are the natural generalization of the anticoordination game to arbitrary numbers of players and actions.

(1) in general, learning strategies based on regret are not well adapted to dispersion games; (2) learning strategies based on best response are well adapted to dispersion problems, but they are not well adapted for learning in the presence of uncertainty; and (3) learning strategies based in the theory of reinforcement learning are the best suited to dispersion games, but they require more computational resources than best response strategies.

(i) the performance of learning strategies in dispersion games is highly dependent on the specific game, and (ii) in some dispersion games, learning agents can achieve near-optimal outcomes, even when they are unable to communicate with each other.
